It also records bounded zero-match split-constant and initialized-pointer searches for the observed vtable base, a bounded OnPressY/OnPressX command-reference chain, a bounded negative for direct uses of the exact GFX_GameSelector.gfx guest string, and a bounded zero-match runtime probe at exact function entry 0x82DECB20. It does not identify the observed receiver's class or visible action owner, either downstream object's class or virtual method semantics, or message or buffer-record semantics, advertisement or discovery behavior, host/client direction, delivery, matchmaking, transport, relay, or Internet play.

currentEvidence.qualification: The visible System Link label owner is UI-only and the visible Refresh and Create Game strings have no modeled references. Exact game-selector AVM1 maps Key.getCode() value 45 to FSCommand:OnPressY and value 42 to FSCommand:OnPressX, and exact guest code recognizes the FSCommand: prefix before two neutral callback sites. One controlled runtime trace observed exact OnPressY at 0x8220B4C0 with receiver 0x509201FC, readable leading word 0x82162F34, and dynamic target 0x82C7CBE0. Static follow-up places that target at vtable slot +0x04 and closes a two-stage virtual-forwarding shape. A second controlled trace at the target observed first virtual target 0x82226AA0, returned-object pointer 0x514BFB90, and second virtual target 0x82E819E0 exactly once. Static identification closes 0x82226AA0 as an argument-object +0xFC word accessor and 0x82E819E0 as a common FSCommand forwarder followed by a conditional object-field +0x430 slot +0x0C dispatch using pointers to two stack temporaries populated by helper calls supplied with the command and neutral argument. A third controlled trace observed that optional dispatch exactly once with object pointer 0x511CECE0 and dynamic target 0x82D76350. A later correlated trace bracketed that exact dispatch with one ordered same-thread marker pair and found zero matching existing-schema XGI/XSession, direct-LAN bind/getname, successful sendto/recvfrom, or QoS lifecycle lines strictly inside it. A separate controlled OnPressX trace bracketed exact indirect call 0x82D765B8, observed neutral dynamic target 0x82D6C340, and found zero matching lines for the same existing schemas strictly inside its one ordered same-thread marker pair. Both bounded negatives exclude no unlogged or asynchronous path. The runtime and static results identify no object class, field semantic, downstream method semantic, visible game-list owner, or networking behavior. The vtable base has zero modeled direct references, zero bounded same-block split-constant constructions, and zero aligned initialized-memory pointer placements. Those negatives exhaust the tested direct static forms without excluding a derived value, copied pointer, unrepresented relocation, indirect producer, or runtime store. Matching OnPressY and OnPressX resource and guest-image strings provide search guidance into exact function 0x82DECB20, but its bounded command chain does not implement or dispatch either command. Exact guest string GFX_GameSelector.gfx has no modeled reference, bounded split-address code use, or aligned initialized-memory pointer placement. A corrected default-off runtime probe at exact function entry 0x82DECB20 produced no matching line during one controlled System Link game-list Y press and captured no receiver identity. Exact message 0x000B001B is submitted with the fixed-size buffer later consumed as the input record collection for the QoS lookup path, but one controlled default-off runtime probe produced no matching request and Xbox static evidence does not prove that the message populates the buffer or name either one.

qosLookup.resultSlot: Before lookup, object slot +0x98C is initialized to object address +0x96C. The cleanup path later passes the slot value to NetDll_XNetQosRelease when non-null; whether lookup replaces the pointer and how release treats it remain unresolved.

qosResultLifecycle.progressGate: A null result bypasses this gate. For a non-null result, a zero word permits the enclosing state field to advance from literal 2 to literal 3; a nonzero word retains state 2.

Exact state function 0x82C9D338 later uses that buffer's leading count to feed QoS lookup producer 0x82C99628, then gates progress on neutral QoS result word +0x04. One controlled default-off runtime probe did not reach the exact request. Exact game-selector AVM1 proves that key-code values 45 and 42 produce FSCommand:OnPressY and FSCommand:OnPressX respectively. The accepted OnPressY runtime chain reaches callback target 0x82C7CBE0, downstream targets 0x82226AA0 and 0x82E819E0, and optional-dispatch target 0x82D76350. Packet 54 identifies 0x82D76350 as a local command-gating body with no direct platform or networking edge. The accepted two-instance Stage 1 LAN run established distinct identities and native binds but no new XGI, socket, sendto, or recvfrom activity for the mapped Refresh action. Later OnPressY and OnPressX correlations each produced one exact marker pair and zero matching existing-schema XGI/XSession, direct-LAN bind/getname, successful sendto/recvfrom, or QoS lifecycle lines strictly inside it. The OnPressX pair observed neutral target 0x82D6C340. Packet 55 identifies that target as an exact modeled five-instruction tail dispatch through incoming-object vtable slot +0x1C with literal argument 11 and no direct platform or networking edge. A separately controlled trace then observed neutral tail target 0x82D704F0 exactly once before normal exit. Packet 56 identifies 0x82D704F0 as an exact modeled neutral state-transition body that conditionally updates global-owned fields and may tail-dispatch through another object's vtable slot +0x0C, again with no direct platform or networking edge. These results establish no object class, field, slot or literal semantic, target method, object ownership, visible action owner, message or record meaning, session creation, advertisement, discovery, delivery, or ordering.
